findings.summary: The holdout diagnosis proved bad controls land silently because approve never runs a verifier against them, and reading three confirmed they are broken controls (not verifier over-flags) — so the FP number measures control-authoring quality. The fix requires SUPERSEDING bad bodies rather than editing them (the corpus is hash-pinned immutable — a Codex-review P0). This increment lands the register-schema foundation that supersession needs.
findings.disposition: The plant register migrated from 5 to 7 cells, adding `status` (current/legacy-invalid/known-overflag/asymmetric) + `supersedes`. parse_register accepts legacy 5-cell rows (-> status=current) AND 7-cell rows; a 6-cell half-migrated row still REFUSES (the silently-dropped-column guarantee holds); format_register_row's defaults keep existing 5-arg callers emitting valid `current` rows; form_problems validates the status vocabulary and rejects dangling/self supersede links. Nine red-first tests plus a regression that the REAL public register still parses + validates (back-compat). This is D0 part 1 of the twice-Codex-reviewed holdout control-validation plan (~/.claude/plans/polymorphic-gathering-rainbow.md); the status->scorer partition, reporting split, per-run population snapshot, the D1 validation gate, the D2 control-quality judge, the D3 authoring-prompt fix, and the D4 supersession remediation remain — carried in a detailed handoff for a fresh session. The commit also lands session calibration telemetry.
